implementation_constraints: Prefer a shared print pattern. Current shared print CSS uses fixed table layout and overflow-wrap:anywhere; the screen wide-table minimum width is 860px.
Preserve portrait Letter as the acceptance target. The open landscape question does not independently authorize abandoning portrait readability.
Preserve every identifier, visible content relationship, table header association, accessible region name, focus stop and screen scrolling behavior.
Keep changes within the exact allowed paths; obtain a revised preparation packet before expanding scope.
Preserve existing provenance and unrelated checkout changes.

required_gates.requirement: Coordinator admission and distinct Ready -> Starting -> Running provider transitions precede implementation. Reconcile current crisis authority; do not invoke claims while prohibited.

Review the proposed shared print treatment against all canonical requirements before implementation. Retain portrait readability, complete identifiers and unchanged screen behavior as separate acceptance criteria.

Produce before-and-after Letter portrait print evidence for the six-column mapping table. Inspect actual printed pages for improved scanability and complete identifiers; verify all six wide tables remain within print margins without clipping.
Verify desktop and narrow-screen rendering, keyboard horizontal scrolling, visible focus, table semantics and accessible names. Check links, fragments, resources and console output for new errors.

Run the selected design-system suite and inspect directly affected shared-style consumers. Add focused assertions for the chosen print behavior and preserved semantics. Record exact changed-path whitespace evidence.

Require independent source review, artifact acceptance, applicable Documentation Design System review and browser-based UX verification against the final candidate. Supply the complete Shared checklist inventory and expected suite navigation when invoking that review; do not substitute unit-test success for these gates.
An independent verifier challenges acceptance against the complete canonical item and verifies the exact reviewed bytes. Missing print or browser evidence remains unfinished.

Apply deliver-work-item-main-branch: accepted commit, resolved required findings, source checks, deliberate integration, focused integrated verification, exact main observation and reachability or content-equivalent integration mapping. Refresh evidence when integration changes reviewed bytes or rendering assumptions.
Only after delivery returns READY may the owning Dev Orchestrator perform the separate file-provider terminal transaction and verify its committed archive outcome.

verification_limit: Catalog commands cover source regressions and whitespace, not visual print or browser acceptance. Those remain mandatory independent execution gates; this preparation does not claim they passed.
